newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent per lb weaker on Tuesday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, dealers said.

Trade is expected to remain rangebound ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply and demand report, released Thursday at 0830 EDT. There are no changes expected from the last report, however.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture said on Monday that 59 percent of the U.S. cotton crop was in good to excellent condition, compared with 57 percent last year.
NYCE reported that the speculators held a net short position of 12.3 percent as of June 6, down slightly from the previous week.
On Monday, July cotton closed down 0.25 cent at 72.12 cents per lb, having traded from 72.60 to 71.90 cents. New crop December went out 0.31 cent lower at 74.74 cents.
